bugs_found: apply_fee: condition 'fee >= fmax' caps fee at fmax even when fee equals fmax (harmless) but combined with wording 'subtle boundary' suggests off-by-one; should be 'fee > fmax' for clarity, though semantically equivalent at equality
apply_fee: missing validation that fee_pct is reasonable (e.g., <= 1 if expected as fraction) - silent acceptance of pct > 1
loan_payment: when r == 0 returns p / m as Decimal division which may yield non-terminating decimal causing precision issues; no explicit rounding/quantization
loan_payment: principal == 0 returns 0 but no early-exit; minor
compound_interest: allows principal to be negative without validation (only rate/years/n are checked)
transfer: not atomic - if second assignment fails after first (unlikely with Decimal but possible with custom types), funds disappear; no transaction/rollback
transfer: uses 'is' identity check instead of comparing account.id, so two Account objects with same id would not be detected as self-transfer
fx_convert: rate is fetched from dict without validating it is positive/non-zero
fx_convert: no support for inverse rate lookup (from,to) missing but (to,from) present
apply_fee: does not quantize result to currency precision (e.g., 2 decimals), can return long Decimal tails
No monetary rounding policy applied anywhere (ROUND_HALF_EVEN / quantize) - finance code should pin precision
Account.balance and amounts are not validated to be Decimal at construction; mixing float could cause precision bugs
No type hints on function signatures despite being finance-critical code
Receipt does not record currency, timestamp, or fee - insufficient audit trail for financial transactions
